description: A ground-level photograph depicts a coastal construction site featuring multiple multi-storey residential buildings in various stages of completion. The buildings are primarily light-coloured (beige/tan) with terracotta-tiled roofs. One building on the right has visible window openings and what appears to be incomplete exterior cladding, while another on the left shows exposed balconies and structural elements. In the midground, an oval-shaped blue swimming pool, partially filled, is visible. Extensive earthworks are present around the buildings and pool, with large piles of excavated soil. A small brick shed is located near the pool, and a stone retaining wall with some climbing vegetation is also visible. The foreground shows disturbed earth with sparse, low vegetation. In the background, a body of water, likely the sea, stretches to the horizon, with a hazy distant city skyline along the coastline, indicating significant development pressure in a coastal environment. The scene illustrates land transformation due to construction, including soil excavation and infrastructure development.
